---
title: "Detection"
subtitle: "The ladder: kernel pre-clear to behavioural bots"
---

Every request walks a fixed, short-circuit-ordered ladder. Earlier stages are cheap; evaluation stops at the first decisive verdict — but every stage consulted emits its verdict as a structured record.

| Stage | Where | Mechanism | Enforces |
|---|---|---|---|
| S0 | kernel | ACL / verdict cache / ban table | drops (`TC_ACT_SHOT`) or fast-path pass |
| S1 | engine | verdict cache re-check | short-circuit |
| S2 | engine | CEL rules (cost-budgeted eval) | block / allow / tag |
| S3 | engine | OWASP CRS via embedded Coraza (PL1+, paranoia configurable) | block / shadow |
| S4 | engine | OpenAPI 3.1 positive security | validate method+path+body invariants |
| S5 | engine | rate-limiting ladder (§13.2) | fixed / sliding-window / token bucket |
| S6 | engine | bots: JA4/JA4S, header order + entropy, behavioural windows | score / ban |

## CRS parity (S3)

Coraza is embedded as the **reference evaluator** — not reimplemented. The `test/crs-differential/` suite replays CRS regression corpora (go-ftw format subset) through both engines and diffs verdicts. The parity gate is **CI-blocking from day one** (M1: 100% applicable rules): parity is why Coraza is embedded, and the differential suite is the mechanism that keeps it honest. A Vectorscan-compiled hot-subset matcher (TR-16) may accelerate the hot regex set, but only behind a shadow-differential gate: never regress vs. the reference evaluator.

## Positive security (S4)

OpenAPI 3.1 specs define method+path+body invariants per route. Routes follow the **promotion-gate discipline** (§14.2.6): `learn` → `shadow` → `enforce`; spec-less routes are discovered in learn mode with drift surfaced as metrics (TR-18). A conforming request passes; a malformed body is rejected with a diagnostic naming the violated field.

## Bots (S6)

JA4/JA4S fingerprints at TLS termination plus header-order and value-entropy checks feed detector verdicts; behavioural window detectors complete the family in TR-19. A curl-vs-browser pair must produce distinct verdicts in lab logs (TR-12 acceptance).

## ScoredWindowBan

The ban engine implements the §13.3 algorithm: a scoring window over weighted violations, with findtime/threshold/bantime parameters. Constraints held from day one:

- evidence record per ban (FP diagnosis in minutes — R11);
- prefix escalation **OFF** by default;
- shadow-first (TR-09 scores and logs would-bans before TR-10 enforces);
- kernel expiry honoured in the ban-table LRU; `BanRelease` supported;
- `BanRateAboveBudget` metric exported.

## Cost budgets (S2)

Every CEL rule evaluates under a per-eval cost budget (buzzer/limit set from the first commit — the §11.3 budget is structurally impossible to skip). Hot reload happens via CRD apply with no restart (TR-17).
